verdicts.reason: Both shrink the three plan cards to unreadable postage stamps (6/48/80 with illegible labels) scattered at random in the left half, and the subtitle is micro-text floating alone, so the pricing message is gone. B is less bad: it keeps the logo at the top-right above a strong headline and a large CTA. A buries the logo at the bottom next to fine print and floats the 48 card on its own between the headline and the CTA.

A has the same flaws as pair 1's B: tiny scattered plan cards and orphaned micro subtitle text on the left, though the right column (logo, headline, CTA) holds together. B is worse: the giant four-line headline takes the centre, the CTA is shrunk and pushed to the right edge beside a ragged block of fine print, and the three tiny cards are flung to three different corners with no grouping or reading order.
